Pembrokeshire: The Coast That Has It All

Pembrokeshire is Wales' premier coastal destination and the UK's only coastal national park. The combination of dramatic cliffs, golden beaches, wildlife-rich islands, and a charming inland countryside makes it one of Britain's finest motorcycle destinations. It's compact enough to explore in a long weekend but rich enough for a full week.

The Coastal Towns

Tenby is Pembrokeshire's jewel — a medieval walled town perched above three golden beaches with pastel-coloured Georgian houses. The harbour is picturesque and the town has excellent restaurants. St David's, Britain's smallest city, has a magnificent cathedral hidden in a valley and a wild, windswept headland. Newport in the north is an understated gem with access to the Preseli Hills.

The Beaches

Pembrokeshire's beaches are world-class:

  • Barafundle Bay — Regularly voted one of Britain's best, accessible only by foot
  • Marloes Sands — Vast beach with dramatic rock formations, relatively uncrowded
  • Whitesands Bay — Surfing beach near St David's, dramatic Ramsey Island views
  • Broad Haven — Family-friendly with good facilities and sunset views
  • Manorbier — Castle overlooking the bay, described as the pleasantest spot in Wales

Wildlife

Pembrokeshire is one of the UK's finest wildlife destinations. Skomer Island (boat trip from Martins Haven) hosts thousands of puffins from May to July. Grey seals haul out on the beaches year-round. Dolphins and porpoises are regularly spotted from cliff-top viewpoints. Ramsey Island has the UK's largest colony of grey seals.

Pembrokeshire is Cornwall without the crowds and at half the price. The scenery is just as spectacular, the beaches are cleaner, and you can actually find a parking space for your motorcycle in summer.

Food and Drink

Pembrokeshire's food scene is excellent. Fresh seafood is the star — Pembrokeshire crab, lobster, and shellfish are superb. The Sloop Inn at Porthgain serves outstanding fish in a converted harbour building. The Shed in Porthgain is a legendary seafood bistro. St David's has several excellent restaurants for a city of 1,600 people.

Practical Information

Pembrokeshire is accessible via the M4 to Carmarthen, then A40 to Haverfordwest — about 4.5 hours from London, 3 from Birmingham, 2 from Bristol. Fuel is available in Tenby, Pembroke, Haverfordwest, and St David's. Accommodation ranges from luxury coastal hotels to campsites and B&Bs. The Pembrokeshire Coast Path (186 miles) follows the entire coast — even short cliff-top sections are spectacular.
keyTakeaways: Pembrokeshire is the UK's only coastal national park, compact enough for a long weekend but rich enough for a full week.
Tenby is the county's jewel, a medieval walled town above three golden beaches, while St David's is Britain's smallest city.
World-class beaches include Barafundle Bay, often voted one of Britain's best, and Marloes Sands.
Skomer Island hosts thousands of puffins from May to July, and Ramsey Island has the UK's largest grey seal colony.
It is roughly 4.5 hours from London via the M4 to Carmarthen then A40 to Haverfordwest.

faq.q: How does Pembrokeshire compare to Cornwall?
faq.a: Pembrokeshire is often described as Cornwall without the crowds and at half the price. The scenery is just as spectacular, the beaches are cleaner and quieter, and you can actually find parking for your motorcycle in summer. As the UK's only coastal national park, it offers dramatic cliffs, golden beaches and wildlife-rich islands.

faq.q: When can I see puffins in Pembrokeshire?
faq.a: Skomer Island, reached by boat trip from Martins Haven, hosts thousands of puffins from May to July, making it one of the UK's finest wildlife destinations. Grey seals haul out on the beaches year-round, dolphins and porpoises are regularly spotted from cliff-tops, and Ramsey Island has the UK's largest grey seal colony.

faq.q: Which are the best beaches in Pembrokeshire?
faq.a: Barafundle Bay is regularly voted one of Britain's best and is accessible only on foot. Marloes Sands is a vast, relatively uncrowded beach with dramatic rock formations, Whitesands Bay near St David's is a fine surfing beach, and Manorbier, overlooked by its castle, has been described as the pleasantest spot in Wales.

faq.q: Where should I eat in Pembrokeshire?
faq.a: Fresh seafood is the star, with superb Pembrokeshire crab, lobster and shellfish. The Sloop Inn at Porthgain serves outstanding fish in a converted harbour building, and The Shed at Porthgain is a legendary seafood bistro. St David's has several excellent restaurants despite a population of just 1,600.

faq.q: How do I get to Pembrokeshire?
faq.a: Pembrokeshire is accessible via the M4 to Carmarthen, then the A40 to Haverfordwest, taking about 4.5 hours from London, three from Birmingham and two from Bristol. Fuel is available in Tenby, Pembroke, Haverfordwest and St David's. Accommodation ranges from luxury coastal hotels to campsites and B&Bs.
